title: vpc-onboarding-runbook-templates-tf-snippets-draft
content:
Purpose:
This working doc collects pragmatic onboarding runbook templates, network reference scenarios, and small Terraform snippets we keep reusing across customer VPC and on-prem Redwood Private installs. Goal: create a single place for a field-ready checklist + code fragments that solutions and infra teams can copy and adapt during onboarding or upgrades.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Solutions engineering, customer SRE, infra, and implementation partners.
- Scope: L3 network design decisions, connectivity patterns (Transit/GW, Direct Connect/VPN, PrivateLink), Terraform snippets for mandatory resources, and upgrade/rollback sequences for control plane/data plane. Not a full tutorial — this is a reusable runbook and paste-ready snippets collection.

Assumptions (common):
- Customer cloud: AWS primary; snippets annotated with equivalents where applicable for GCP/Azure.
- Customer provides a VPC with 3 AZ subnets for data plane workers and at least one management subnet for control-plane private endpoints.
- BGP/Direct Connect or Transit Gateway available for low-latency enterprise connections.
- Customer will accept IAM role trust for a cross-account deploy agent (standard for Dedicated/Private installs).

Quick onboarding scenarios (pick one):
1) Basic isolated VPC (small teams, limited traffic)
   - Single VPC, public egress through NAT, no customer-managed transit.
   - Use security groups to lock access to control-plane endpoints.
   - TF snippet: create peered endpoint + route-table entries (see snippet A).
2) Enterprise transit (recommended for scale)
   - Transit Gateway (TGW) or cloud-native hub; customer attaches branch networks and DX to the TGW.
   - Use TGW route tables to isolate management/control subnets from application subnets.
   - PrivateLink for control-plane endpoints to avoid cross-account routing complexity.
3) On-prem/air-gapped (regulated)
   - Private control plane with customer-hosted bastion + OOB management network.
   - Offline image/installer and HSM/KMS integration required.

Network layout decision checklist (short):
- CIDR sizing: reserve /20 for data plane per cluster; avoid overlapping with company-wide networks.
- AZ placement: minimum 3 AZs for HA where available.
- NAT/Egress: decide centralized NAT vs per-subnet NAT gateway (cost vs blast radius).
- Service endpoints: prefer PrivateLink for cross-account control-plane endpoints.
- DNS: split-horizon private hosted zone recommended for control-plane hostnames.

Terraform snippets (copy/paste and adapt)
- Snippet A: VPC peering + route table entry (AWS, minimal)
resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection" "rw_peering" {
  provider = aws.customer
  vpc_id   = var.customer_vpc_id
  peer_vpc_id = var.platform_vpc_id
  auto_accept = true
  tags = { Name = "redwood-platform-peering" }
}

resource "aws_route" "to_platform" {
  provider = aws.customer
  route_table_id = var.customer_route_table_id
  destination_cidr_block = var.platform_vpc_cidr
  vpc_peering_connection_id = aws_vpc_peering_connection.rw_peering.id
}

Notes: ensure security-group egress/ingress allow required ports (TLS 443, KV cache ports if used).

- Snippet B: TGW attachment (recommended for large customers)
resource "aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment" "tgw_attach" {
  transit_gateway_id = var.tgw_id
  vpc_id = var.customer_vpc_id
  subnet_ids = var.subnet_ids
  tags = { Name = "rw-tgw-attach" }
}

- Snippet C: Interface VPC Endpoint for control-plane (AWS PrivateLink)
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "platform_api" {
  vpc_id = var.customer_vpc_id
  service_name = var.platform_endpoint_service_name
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids = var.management_subnets
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.endpoint_sg.id]
}

Security group recommendation: allow only TLS from customer admin IP ranges and platform subnet CIDRs.

Upgrade plan (control plane + data plane)
Principles: automated, incremental, observable, reversible.
Pre-upgrade steps (1-2 weeks before production update):
- Lock down a dedicated test VPC that mirrors production topology.
- Smoke test: full install + basic workload run and E2E latency checks.
- Create a formal rollout plan (canary thresholds, MTTI targets).
- Backup: export configs, DB snapshot (if applicable), KV cache dump.

Control plane upgrade (canary-first):
1) Push new control-plane container to canary namespace in test VPC. Run health checks for 30m.
2) If healthy, roll to a single customer management subnet (non-prod) for staged validation.
3) Roll to remaining management subnets with 15–30m observation windows.
4) Finalize by notifying customer and flipping routing (if any) to new endpoints.

Data plane upgrade (rolling, per-AZ):
- Strategy: drain small batch of workers (5–10% depending on cluster size), upgrade, health-check, then continue.
- KV/Cache warmup: pre-warm caches or rely on gradual regeneration to avoid thundering herd.
- If using kernel/quantization changes, test on low-traffic nodes first.

Rollback plan (fast path):
- Control plane: revert DNS pointer to previous endpoint; scale old control-plane deployment back up; restore DB snapshot only if schema incompatible.
- Data plane: use autoscaling group or k8s rollout to scale back to previous version.

Post-upgrade verification checklist:
- Endpoint TLS handshake successful (third-party test): PASS
- P50/P95 tail latency within expected delta: PASS/FAIL
- Token cost per request check (sanity): within 15% of baseline
- Audit logs intact and accessible for last 48h

Troubleshooting quick hits (common issues):
- Peering routes not visible: check route table association and peering TA status.
- PrivateLink SG blocking: temporary allow all from platform subnets for smoke test, then tighten.
- BGP flaps after upgrade: ensure ASNs unchanged and route maps preserved.

Templates / Copyable checklists (use in pre-flight email to customer):
- Network preflight: CIDRs, AZs, NAT choice, transit/peering model, endpoint type, route tables, NACLs
- IAM: deploy role ARN, deploy agent IP ranges, cross-account trust policy snippet (attach link)
- Certificates: who manages TLS certs for private endpoints? (customer / Redwood)
- Monitoring hooks: ensure CloudWatch/Datadog metrics and log push endpoints configured prior to go-live

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Decide on a default recommendation for NAT (centralized vs per-subnet) based on cost break-even table (owner: Jonah).
- Add GCP/Azure equivalents of PrivateLink and TGW snippets (owner: Claire).
- Convert snippets into module pattern with variables and outputs for reusability in terraform-modules repo.

Next steps (short-term):
- Move approved snippets to terraform-modules PR and add outputs for endpoint ids.
- Create a small automated smoke test harness that consumes the runbook checklist and runs a health-check pipeline for new installs.
- Schedule a brown-bag with Solutions + SRE to align on common customer templates.

Appendix: useful links and references:
- Confluence: VPC Patterns Index (link in metadata)
- GitHub: terraform-modules repo (linked in metadata)
- Example ticket: JIRA-1258 (customer: Acme Corp - TGW onboarding)

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep each snippet intentionally small — prefer composition over a giant module.
- When in doubt use PrivateLink for control-plane endpoints to simplify customer routing constraints.
- Capture a short video walkthrough of the preflight checklist for the onboarding playbook.

End of draft.
